items.quote: but if not, then let fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon!
items.contrast: The reader must distinguish the consequence of rejecting the thornbush from the invitation to take refuge in its shade if it is accepted.
items.reason: The conditional contrast clearly assigns fire consuming the cedars to the trees’ failure to accept the thornbush as king. Taking refuge in its shade belongs to the opposite condition.
